messages:
cheng: Quick summary from the staging concurrency sweep (g5x2 pool): p99 latency spikes correlate tightly with KV cache eviction storms under high concurrency. Short dump below with actionable numbers.

profiling-snapshot:
concurrency=800 -> throughput=440 req/s
p50=22ms p95=130ms p99=420ms
kv_hit_rate=87.4% (idle) -> 42.6% (under load)
eviction_rate=23 evictions/s -> 198 evictions/s at peak
kernel_fallback_count=540 (fused->generic)

zach: ouch. microbatching config? were you capping depth or tokens?

cheng: microbatch_max=16, dynamic batching enabled. We saw p99 reduced when microbatch_max increased to 32 but p95 moved up a bit — classic latency SLO vs throughput tradeoff. Also kernel selector started choosing non-fused kernel under CPU pressure which added ~30-50ms per call.

elaine: interesting — kernel fallback usually happens when we hit memory/threads contention. For short seqs (<128) fused-attn is still faster; we may be misdetecting due to noisy perf samples under high concurrency. Could force kernel selection as an experiment.

devon: KV side: eviction storms suggest a hotset thrash. Have you tried SLRU or adding a small victim cache to absorb bursts? Also async prefetch on miss helps when miss latency dominates.

cheng: we prototyped SLRU yesterday — hit_rate improved to ~62% at same concurrency and p99 dropped to ~210ms in quick A run. Caveat: eviction writeback was contending with CPU and causing sporadic 100-200ms stalls for some requests. Need to isolate eviction IO.

infra-bot: alert: staging/g5x2 observed >150% eviction rate over baseline at 2026-11-18T10:03Z (auto-collected).

perf-bot: summary test results:
A (baseline LRU, microbatch=16): p99=420ms, throughput=440 r/s
B (LRU, microbatch=32): p99=280ms, throughput=520 r/s
C (SLRU + microbatch=32): p99=210ms, throughput=510 r/s

zach: those numbers are promising. Next steps: instrument per-request kv_latency + queue_length and emit histograms so we can see if tail is due to single slow kv access or queueing/backpressure. Also add a p99 circuit that routes to a lower-capacity model variant if tail breaches.

elaine: batching heuristic idea: add a latency-first mode where we cap batch depth based on observed p95 target. Example policy: prefer 95th bound < 120ms even if throughput drops 10-20%.

cheng: config snippet I used in the SLRU run:
```
batching:
  policy: dynamic
  latency_slo_ms: 120
  microbatch_max: 32
kv_cache:
  policy: slru
  hot_ratio: 0.2
  victim_size: 512
  prefetch_on_miss: true
kernel_selector:
  override_short_seq: fused-attn
  fallback_threshold_ms: 50
```

devon: action items (short):
- A: run full A/B at 1k concurrency comparing LRU vs SLRU (stress eviction IO)
- B: isolate eviction writer to a dedicated CPU (reduce stalls) + measure effect
- C: add per-core eviction_queue_length metric + kv_latency histograms and alerts (p95/p99)
- D: test kernel selector override for seq<128 under load

cheng: I'll kick off A & B now and push traces to s3: s3://redwood-perf/kv-eviction/1763505600-run1.tar.gz. Will post raw perf traces + flame graphs when available. tagging @zach @elaine for review. :rocket:

zach: ack. please include the microbench harness and the exact seed so we can reproduce. Also track memory pressure during runs.

elaine: if SLRU + kernel override looks stable, we should add a rollout plan: canary with 5% traffic, monitor p99, kv_hit, eviction_rate for 1 hour, then 25%, etc.

cheng: agreed — will draft the canary steps after the A/B. For now I want to confirm eviction IO is the final culprit. If so, we may need a small rewrite of eviction writer to be lock-free.

devon: nice. also consider short-term mitigation: increase KV cache capacity for high-tier customers or pin hot keys for critical routes.

cheng: noted. uploading traces now — will update thread when results complete.
